page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-32-lssd is an enterprise compute instance designed for memory-intensive workloads that require rapid local disk performance. The server is powered by a 64-bit x86 architecture and features 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 252 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory allocation of approximately 7.88 GB per vCPU. This elevated memory density positions the instance to support applications that handle substantial in-memory state without experiencing memory exhaustion or excessive swap activity.

Storage capability is provided via 805 GB of integrated local NVMe solid-state storage spread across two physical drives. This local disk configuration delivers high IOPS and low I/O latency compared to remote network block storage, making it effective for scratch spaces, local indexing, or transactional databases requiring minimal disk access overhead. The instance operates without discrete GPU hardware accelerators and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing its operational profile strictly toward CPU processing, memory utilization, and local disk throughput.

From an architectural tradeoff perspective, the fixed 805 GB local NVMe storage requires external replication or snapshot strategies for durable storage needs, as local SSDs are ephemeral across machine stop operations. The density of dedicated cores paired with 252 GB of RAM provides cost-efficient operational consolidation for services that would otherwise require multiple smaller instances. Primary workload fits include high-throughput relational and NoSQL databases, in-memory caching platforms, real-time analytics engines, and data transformation pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-32-lssd is a memory-oriented compute instance configured with 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 252 GB of system memory, delivering roughly 7.88 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 805 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage across two drives, ensuring low-latency data access directly on the host. Lacking discrete GPUs, the configuration is tailored specifically for CPU-bound, memory-dense workloads that benefit from fast local storage. This profile provides an efficient balance for memory-heavy services by combining substantial memory capacity with direct-attached NVMe storage, eliminating external network storage bottlenecks for high-throughput processing. Optimal deployments include in-memory databases, distributed caching nodes, transactional database management systems, and intensive ETL pipelines that require large active memory footprints and rapid temporary storage.
